entry.title: Vectors: components, addition, dot and cross products
entry.summary: A vector carries a magnitude and a direction. Split it into components and the algebra falls out: addition, scaling, the dot product for angles, the cross product for area and torque.

entry.title: How does a ball accelerate toward a target?
entry.summary: Acceleration is how fast velocity changes. Point a constant acceleration at a target and the ball speeds up, overshoots, then loops back — here is why, with a simulation to try.

entry.title: How does a spring work?
entry.summary: A spring pushes back in proportion to how far you stretch it — that is Hooke's law, and it is exactly what makes a mass on a spring oscillate. Here is the physics, with a simulation.

entry.title: How does projectile motion work?
entry.summary: Gravity pulls a projectile straight down while its sideways speed stays constant. Those two independent motions combine into a parabola — here is the maths, with an interactive launcher.

entry.title: The Three-Body Problem: The Equation That Broke Physics
entry.summary: Two bodies orbiting under gravity are perfectly predictable; three are chaotic. Why the three-body problem has no formula — and what the Netflix show gets right and wrong.

entry.title: How Two Sliding Blocks Compute π — The Most Surprising Result in Physics
entry.summary: Two frictionless blocks and a wall, all collisions elastic: count the clacks and you get the digits of π. The physics behind it, from the first collision to the geometric proof.

entry.title: What Is Physics? A Visual, Interactive Introduction for Beginners
entry.summary: Physics explained visually — not just with formulas. Discover the major branches of physics, real-world applications, and explore free interactive simulations to see the science in action.

entry.title: The Physics of the Pendulum: This is How It Works
entry.summary: An exhaustive exploration of pendulum dynamics from elementary observations to advanced nonlinear analysis, encompassing simple harmonic motion, energy conservation, chaotic behavior, and quantum mechanical interpretations.
